report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of graph_delta.py: function_deltas, specificity, measure_commit, commit_shas, _refs_by_function, _int_arg, and the mutation measurement loop. Claims checked against visible code.
risks: measure_commit line 599 | high | _type_edge_keys is called but not defined in this chunk; may be missing or imported from elsewhere; if absent, runtime error. | Verify _type_edge_keys is defined or imported in the full file.

specificity line 627-628 | medium | _refs_by_function uses ast.walk on each function body, which may be O(n^2) for large files; not a correctness risk but performance. | Assess performance on large files.

measure_commit line 597 | medium | before/after parsing for each file may fail silently; if _ast_refs raises an unhandled exception, the loop may crash. | Confirm _ast_refs error handling covers all cases.

function_deltas line 670 | low | The docstring says 'functions added or removed wholesale are excluded', but the code uses set intersection; this is correct, but if a function is renamed, it appears as added+removed and is excluded from rows. | Confirm intent.
_int_arg line 575 | low | Silent fallback on malformed input is intentional per docstring, but may hide configuration errors. | Acceptable per docstring.

claims.text: An unparsable half is not a detection and not a failure of the detector; counting it either way would move the headline for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: The try-except catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError and continues without incrementing detected or n.

claims.text: ``--limit 40``, or the default. Silent fallback is deliberate: a malformed limit should not lose the run, and the value is echoed in the written report either way.
claims.why: Code returns default on ValueError or IndexError; no exception propagates.

claims.text: The mutation corpus contains only BAD patches, so it measures sensitivity and cannot measure specificity at all.
claims.why: The comment states the limitation; the specificity arm addresses it with real commits.

claims.text: A signal that moves for every change discriminates nothing.
claims.why: This is a statement of principle, not a checkable claim; code does not contradict.

claims.text: This arm runs REAL COMMITS through the identical pipeline so the two distributions can be compared.
claims.why: specificity() and measure_commit() implement the real commit pipeline.

claims.text: five of the seven detected mutations were PURE DELETIONS (``+0/-N``). Seeded defects disable things — they remove a guard, a call, a check — while real work usually adds or exchanges.
claims.why: This refers to a prior result not present in this chunk; no code here confirms or denies.

claims.text: So the candidate discriminator is not "did the delta move" but "did it move in the DELETING direction only".
claims.why: The hypothesis is not implemented in this chunk; specificity() does not implement this discriminator.

claims.text: Non-merge commits touching Python, newest first. Merges are excluded because a merge's diff against its first parent attributes other people's work to it, which would pollute the corpus with changes it did not make.
claims.why: Code uses '--no-merges' and '--' with paths '*.py'; order is newest first per git log default.

claims.text: The same layer delta, for one real commit. Returns per-file and totals.
claims.why: Function computes added, removed, type_moved per file and aggregates.

claims.text: A sweeping commit would dominate the distribution for a reason that has nothing to do with defectiveness. Bounded and SAID, never silently cut.
claims.why: Code checks len(files) > max_files and sets skipped reason with file count; returns early.

claims.text: Per-FUNCTION reference multisets. The granularity a defect actually has.
claims.why: Function walks AST, groups by function, returns Counter per function name.

claims.text: Aggregating a delta per commit was wrong and the measurement showed it: this repository's history is nearly all growth (median +354 references per commit, median -0), so any "removed vs added" rule is trivially never true at commit scale, and a guard deleted beside a new 300-line module is invisible.
claims.why: The claim about historical medians is not present in this chunk; no code confirms or denies.

claims.text: A seeded defect edits ONE function; so the comparison has to be one function wide or the signal drowns in the rest of the patch.
claims.why: function_deltas implements per-function comparison by intersecting function names.

claims.text: One row per function that exists in BOTH versions and changed.
claims.why: Code uses set intersection (fb.keys() & fa.keys()) and iterates over sorted intersection.

claims.text: Functions added or removed wholesale are excluded: a new function has no 'before' to lose references against, and counting it as a huge addition would swamp the distribution the rule is read from.
claims.why: Code only processes names in intersection; added/removed functions are not in both, so excluded.

observations.what: _type_edge_keys is called in measure_commit but not defined in this chunk; may be defined earlier in the file or imported.
The mutation measurement loop uses _ast_refs, _literal_keys, _structure_keys which are defined earlier in the file; no issue.
specificity returns 'rows' containing full per-file data; could be large but is documented.
_refs_by_function qualifies functions by name only, not by line number; if two methods have same name (e.g., overloaded) they are merged.
